name: Uvinul T 150 (ethylhexyl triazone)

lead: Uvinul T 150 is a UVB filter used in some sunscreens, mainly outside the US, where it helps reach higher SPF values.
Published work is mostly formulation tests and environmental monitoring; no clinical studies were found.

paras: It absorbs UVB light (peak near 314 nm) and is described as photostable.
No human clinical safety trials were found in the sources reviewed. Environmental studies have detected triazine filters in sediment, dust and tested aquatic organisms.

lead: Ethylhexyl triazone, marketed by BASF as Uvinul T 150, is an oil-soluble organic UVB filter used in sunscreens, typically to raise SPF.[1] A Grokipedia summary reports an absorption peak near 314 nm, a permitted EU level of up to 5 percent, and no approval as a US sunscreen active.[1]

Published work involving the ingredient is mainly product-testing and environmental. A 2011 study compared fifteen European sunscreens of identical label SPF under natural sunlight, and environmental studies have measured triazine UV filters in sediments, indoor dust and marine organisms.[2][3][4][5]
infobox: Not an approved sunscreen active per the cited source[1]

paras: The molecule is a symmetric tris-anilino-triazine with three ethylhexyl ester groups, which makes it highly lipophilic and water-insoluble according to the AI-generated Grokipedia entry.[1]

A 2011 study tested fifteen marketed European sunscreens with the same label SPF but different filter combinations under natural sunlight and reported differing photoprotection and photostability, calling for harmonised photostability and UVA labelling.[2] A 2021 review asked whether sunscreens have progressed over two decades.[6] Studies of ferulic acid and lipid nanoparticle systems used combinations of organic filters in formulation research.[7][8]

A 2018 North and Baltic Sea sediment survey, a 2020 study on brine shrimp and microalgae, and a 2022 study of indoor dust and air in South China reported detecting triazine filters or testing their effects.[3][4][5] Grokipedia also mentions environmental persistence concerns.[1]
No studies found. Research on the filter consists of laboratory, product-testing and environmental studies.
